excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
thx for the api specs!
I've hooked up the new endpoints to dora. I've also seen teku is already emitting the new event - nice work 🙂

I'm not gonna push the latest dora changes to the eip7732-support branch yet to not break it. 
The beacon api to load execution envelopes from seems not supported by teku/prysm yet. that breaks the finalization in dora as it repeatedly tries to fetch the missing information (canonical finalized blocks normally must have a execution payload)
Please ping me if any of you have implemented the api 🙂

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
I'm confused,  how is it possible that a canonical block does not have a payload?
You can't build on a parent block that does not have a payload, right? 
So all blocks without payloads will be orphaned, which means they cannot be part of the canonical chain and can't be finalized too?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: No, that's a feature of ePBS, that the chain can continue without payloads and can even finalize without a single payload

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
oh, interesting. 
But why does your chain look like this when missing a lot of payloads?
If missing payloads are allowed, there shouldn't be any forks,  just "empty" blocks?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: That's a bug in prysm after justification: the chain was fine without payloads up until the new epoch, at this point the forkchoice bug makes any block that comes not be head so regardless of payload or not, the next proposer reorgs it

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I'm focusing now in trying to understand the Teku/Prysm mismatch in the happy case before trying to finalize an unhappy one

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Will get back to that forkchoice bug later on

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
Aaah, got it 🙂 Thx for clarification. 
Gonna rework the dora implementation then 😄

One question left:
How can I be sure that a missing payload is really missing and not just missing due to an RPC issue or so?
Is there any indication in the next block that tells me if the parent had a payload?

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content: Ah yea, I can use the `parent_block_hash` of the `ExecutionPayloadHeader` for it 🙂

can we have "orphaned payloads" in beacon blocks? 
ie. a payload that builds on top of the payload from 2 blocks ago, skipping the payload from the last block
